title: API + MCP: single hybrid retrieval entrypoint with provenance
priority_note: Exposes the hybrid resolver + progressive index to agents over the existing HTTP/MCP surface, so callers get one interface + provenance (no RAG-or-curated branching). Depends on the resolver (31.2) and index (31.3).

background.reference: GitHub issues #305/#306; extends the existing knowledge HTTP API (knowledge_search_controller / knowledge_context_controller) + the mcp-server knowledge_* tools.
background.includes: US-31.2/31.3 provide hybrid_search + progressive disclosure. This story surfaces them: an HTTP endpoint + an MCP tool returning provenance, reusing the existing knowledge API/MCP conventions.

story.as_a: an agent via MCP (or an API client)
story.i_want_to: call one hybrid knowledge tool/endpoint that returns curated-or-retrieved answers with provenance, and a progressive index tool
story.so_that: I use the hybrid interface the same way I use knowledge_search today, but with trustable provenance

rationale: The value of a single hybrid interface is lost if callers must still pick an endpoint. Surfacing hybrid_search (and the progressive index) as one API endpoint + one MCP tool, on the existing authenticated pipeline, is what delivers 'no caller-side RAG-or-curated branching' to real agents.

acceptance_criteria.description: An HTTP endpoint POST /api/v1/knowledge/hybrid_search (on the :authenticated pipeline) resolves tenant_id from conn.assigns and calls Loopctl.Knowledge.hybrid_search(tenant_id, query, opts), returning results + provenance (:curated|:retrieved) + confidence + meta. (POST — vs the existing GET /knowledge/search — is a deliberate divergence for the richer body; OpenAPI operation in the controller + schema in api_spec/, error envelope reused.)

TWO MCP tools are added by the existing two-list convention (calling the endpoints via shared http-helpers + witness-sth): knowledge_hybrid_search (with a docstring explaining provenance and when to prefer it over the knowledge_search tool), AND a progressive-disclosure index/drill tool (US-31.3) so the index half actually reaches agents. Both are required, not optional.
Response provenance is preserved end-to-end (a curated answer is flagged curated at the MCP boundary, retrieved flagged retrieved); existing knowledge_* tools/endpoints are unchanged (additive).
Tenant isolation + witness/custody: the endpoint rides the existing authenticated/witness pipeline; a two-tenant test proves no cross-tenant answer via API or MCP.

test_cases.name: hybrid endpoint returns curated with provenance over HTTP
preconditions: a curated refund-policy article + fuzzy chunks
expected_results: 200 with the curated article, provenance: curated, confidence, meta

test_cases.name: MCP hybrid + progressive-disclosure tools work; static tools unchanged
preconditions: MCP server pointed at the test API; a governed curated article + fuzzy chunks + a linked-hub topic
steps: call the progressive index tool then drill
expected_results: curated answer flagged curated; the index tool returns capped stubs and drill returns a body; existing knowledge_* tools still present + unchanged

test_cases.name: hybrid API/MCP is tenant-isolated
steps: POST /api/v1/knowledge/hybrid_search as key_u for tenant_a's topic

technical_notes: Controller: extend the knowledge controllers (knowledge_search_controller / a new hybrid action); reuse the :authenticated pipeline + error envelope + OpenAPI convention (macro in controller, schema in api_spec/).
MCP: add knowledge_hybrid_search (+ optional index/drill) to mcp-server/index.js by the two-list convention; reuse http-helpers.js + witness-sth.js.
Additive only — do not change existing knowledge_search behavior/shape.
Tests use Loopctl.Fixtures.fixture/2 (fixture(:api_key, tenant:, role:)) + Mox embedding.
